question: Three wires, A, B and C, of the same length and the same thickness have resistances of 1 Ω, 0.5 Ω and 0.25 Ω, respectively. Their resistivities are ________ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**in the ratio of 4 ∶ 2 ∶ 1.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Resistance**

 
 
• **​**Every material has an electrical resistance, which is why conductors** emit heat** when current passes through them.
 
• When an electric **current flows **through a bulb or any conductor, the conductor provides some obstruction to the current. This obstruction is referred to as electrical resistance and is** denoted by R.**
 
• There is a relationship between the **potential difference** across a conductor and the **current** that flows through it, according to **Ohm's law**. It comes from, **V=IR**
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Electrical Resistance**
 
 
• The following factors influence a conductor's **electrical resistance**:
 
 
• The **cross-sectional area** of the conductor
 
• **Length** of the conductor
 
• The **material** of the conductor
 
• The **temperature** of the conducting material
 
 
 
• Electrical resistance is** inversely proportional** to the conductor's cross-sectional area (A) and directly proportional to its length (L). The relationship that follows provides it. 

 **R= ρL/A**

 where** ρ is the material's resistivity**, expressed as m/ohm meter.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calculation**

 
 
• Three wires, A, B and C, of the same length(L) and the same thickness(A) have resistances of 1 Ω, 0.5 Ω and 0.25 Ω, respectively.

 **R₁= 1Ω, R₂= 0.5Ω, R₃= 0.25Ω**

 We know, **R= ρL/A**

 1= ρ₁L/A: 0.5= ρ₂L/A: 0.25= ρ₃L/A

 1= ρ₁: 0.5=ρ₂: 0.25= ρ₃

 1= ρ₁: 1/2= ρ₂: 1/4= ρ₃

 4= ρ₁: 2= ρ₂: 1= ρ₃

 **​So, ρ₁: ρ₂: ρ₃= 4:2:1**
